## RCA (Phase 1) — proven at runtime

**Reproduction (current worktree off origin/main, commit fbfeb40).** Ran the single test
`tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign.py::test_resign_routes_through_pin_collecting_sign_path`
with `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` pointed at an empty scratch dir. The test-call PASSED, and the run
materialized a real on-disk snapshot tree under the gate cache:

- `rebar-gate-snapshots/<code-sha>/`  = 3,393 files (the code tree at HEAD)
- `rebar-gate-snapshots/tickets-<sha>/.tickets-tracker/` = 121,594 files (the tickets branch)
- total: **1.1 GB, 124,994 files**

Deleting that scratch tree with `rm -rf` afterward took ~40s of recursive `unlinkat`/`rmdir`
locally — the exact post-PASS deletion signature the ticket records (minutes on the F12 host,
which has a larger tickets branch / slower FS).

**Mechanism.** `resign.resign_plan_review(ticket_id)` signs inside an attested gate session:
it calls `gate_source.resolve_gate_handle(None, SOURCE_ATTESTED, repo_root, fetch=False)` then
`gate_source.gate_read_root(handle)`. With `repo_root=None` and the autouse conftest fixture
`_gate_source_attested_by_default` (sets `REBAR_GATE_SOURCE=attested`, `REBAR_GATE_REF=HEAD`),
`resolve_gate_handle` materializes the **real** repo tree at HEAD via
`_snapshot.repo_snapshot.materialize` **and** `materialize_tickets` (the 121k-file tickets
branch) into the gate cache. The test monkeypatches the INNER `attest.sign_plan_review`, but
NOT the surrounding `gate_source` seam, so the expensive real materialization runs. Its
creation dominates the test-call time and its later deletion dominates the post-PASS interval.

**Falsifiable hypotheses tested.** (1) Session-finish tmp cleanup as an independent cost —
REJECTED: the tree is created by this test's own call to the gate seam (empty scratch dir
before, 1.1 GB after a single test). (2) Host FS contention — REJECTED: reproduced in an
isolated single-test run. (3) sign-time cost inside `sign_plan_review` — REJECTED:
`sign_plan_review` is monkeypatched to a no-op; the cost is entirely the pre-sign
`resolve_gate_handle`/`materialize_tickets`. Gerrit change 2141 (timeout coverage) only changes
the terminal failure mode, not this phase.

**Defect origin (caused_by).** The test was written 2026-07-21 (32131209ae03) when resign did
NOT materialize a snapshot. Bug **5128-0856-d80f-4eb6** (commit 1e7e5c9468f8, 2026-07-24)
wrapped resign's sign step in a real attested gate session (`resolve_gate_handle` +
`gate_read_root`), which turned the pre-existing routing unit test into one that materializes
the real 121k-file tickets snapshot. The two sibling tests added for that work
(`test_public_resign_preserves_authenticated_none_scope`,
`test_public_resign_preserves_mixed_child_scope_and_validity`) DO stub
`gate_source.resolve_gate_handle`/`gate_read_root`; the routing test was never retrofitted with
that same stub. This is a test-isolation defect, not a production defect — in production the
snapshot cache is content-addressed and reused, and reclaimed by the GC trigger.

**Fix direction.** Sandbox the routing test by stubbing `gate_source.resolve_gate_handle` and
`gate_read_root` (the established sibling pattern), so no real snapshot is materialized. RED-first
oracle: with an empty `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR`, the unpatched test populates the cache (materialization
reached); the fixed test leaves it empty and runs sub-second.

## Phase 2 — RED-first fix (proven)

**Fix.** `tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign.py::test_resign_routes_through_pin_collecting_sign_path`
now stubs `gate_source.resolve_gate_handle` (returns a benign handle, records the call) and
`gate_source.gate_read_root` (nullcontext) — the exact isolation the two sibling public-resign
tests already apply. A `gate_handle_calls` spy asserts resign still routes signing through the
attested gate seam, so the sandbox does not mask a routing regression.

**RED-first oracle (empirical).** With `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` at an empty scratch dir:
- RED (stubs removed = pre-fix behavior): a bounded 22s run materialized **62,984** real
  snapshot files (climbing toward the full 124,994 / 1.1 GB) before being killed mid-write —
  the real HEAD code tree + 121k-file tickets branch. This is the multi-minute post-PASS
  `unlinkat`/`rmdir` deletion the ticket reports.
- GREEN (fixed): the same single test passes in ~5.6s and materializes **0** files.

**Suite.** Full `tests/unit/test_plan_review_resign.py` = 8 passed in 18.76s (previously the one
test alone was ~200s call + minutes of cleanup). `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass. Unrelated
test behavior preserved (only this test's isolation changed; the three sibling resign tests and
their gate stubs are untouched).

**Attribution.** caused_by 5128-0856-d80f-4eb6 (commit 1e7e5c9468f8) — added the attested gate
session to resign; the routing test was never retrofitted with the sibling gate stub.

## Relationship to related tickets (AC4)
- **grindable-deviant-angwantibo** / **asbestos-popular-tench** (closed): fixed omitted private `--basetemp` in NESTED pytest CHILDREN. Distinct: this delay is in an ORDINARY in-process session with no nested pytest child — it is gate-snapshot materialization, not a basetemp propagation bug.
- **famished-disgustful-gypsymoth** (active): changes timeout coverage for fixture phases. Distinct: the cost here is in the test CALL (resign materialization) + post-PASS deletion, not a fixture-phase timeout; it records neither this test nor the deletion interval.
- **expectable-slowwitted-squeaker** (active): a local Git child timeout. Distinct: no local Git child is spawned on resign's sign path; the cost is filesystem materialize/rmtree of the gate snapshot.
- **Gerrit change 2141** (timeout coverage): guards only the terminal failure MODE, not this materialization phase; it would not prevent the multi-minute materialize/delete.
None of these record this test or its post-PASS deletion interval, so the fix is independent (a test-isolation stub in test_plan_review_resign.py).

## Context
F12 verification on commit 8a036765705f5ef0e7db4fa21e0926e51d15bafd exposed a long-running `test_resign_routes_through_pin_collecting_sign_path`. An isolated run on current `origin/main` commit 51621917bfc635d7673cb0519a400afda12eb2cb reproduced the delay. The test body reported PASS after 201.81 seconds. The process exited after 524.52 seconds. Pytest attributed 5.15 seconds to setup and 0.06 seconds to teardown. A one-second process sample during the remaining post-PASS interval showed recursive filesystem deletion dominated by `unlinkat` and `rmdir`.

Closed tickets `grindable-deviant-angwantibo` and `asbestos-popular-tench` repaired omitted private `--basetemp` arguments in nested pytest children. This reproduction occurs in an ordinary test session and needs separate lifecycle tracing. Active ticket `famished-disgustful-gypsymoth` changes timeout coverage for fixture phases. Active ticket `expectable-slowwitted-squeaker` covers a local Git child timeout. Neither ticket records this test or its post-PASS deletion interval.

## Plan
- Reproduce the delay in an isolated current-main worktree and capture phase timings, the active temporary path, file counts, allocated bytes, and a Python stack during the post-PASS interval.
- Trace the fixture and pytest lifecycle that creates and removes the snapshot tree.
- Distinguish test-call snapshot materialization cost, session-finish cleanup cost, shared temporary-root cleanup, and host filesystem contention with discriminating experiments.
- Determine whether pending Gerrit change 2141 guards the affected phase or only changes the terminal failure mode.
- Establish the intended behavior from the maintained timeout and test-runtime policy.
- Confirm the root cause and defect origin before proposing any repair.
- If a repair is warranted, update this ticket with the fix plan and file impact, obtain a current plan review, and prove the repair with a RED-first held-out oracle.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A current-main reproduction records call time, total time, and the post-PASS stack.
- [x] Runtime evidence identifies the lifecycle phase and the changeable artifact responsible for the delay.
- [x] Discriminating experiments reject the surviving alternative explanations.
- [x] The relationship to `grindable-deviant-angwantibo`, `asbestos-popular-tench`, `famished-disgustful-gypsymoth`, and `expectable-slowwitted-squeaker` is recorded.
- [x] The defect origin is proven or the RCA records the completed unattributable search.
- [x] The RCA is recorded before any repair begins.
- [x] Any repair uses a RED-first oracle, preserves unrelated test behavior, and passes its declared verification.
